Home News Arts and Culture Business Sports Opinion Research Live TV/Radio Media Elections Dark Mode Dark mode --> National President Mahama commends Ghana EXIM Bank for supporting local industries Source : Albert Kuzor 16 November 2026 5:44pm ▶ Listen to this article Audio By Carbonatix
President John Dramani Mahama has commended the Ghana Export-Import Bank (Ghana EXIM Bank) for its role in financing local industries and supporting the establishment of factories to create employment opportunities.
He said the bank was making significant contributions to the government's industrialisation agenda by providing financial support to businesses involved in manufacturing and agro-processing.
Speaking just before he commissioned EXIM Bank-funded NADKANSCO Cashew Processing Limited in Techiman North on Monday, November 16, 2026, President Mahama praised the bank for its interventions in helping local businesses complete and operationalise factories.
“Let me commend Ghana EXIM for what they are doing. In three months, this is the second time they pulled me out to commission a factory,” he said.
He cited the bank's support for a factory in Savelugu, in the Northern Region, which had stalled after its initial financing arrangements proved insufficient.
According to the President, Ghana EXIM Bank intervened by taking over the financing arrangement, providing additional funding to complete the facility and consolidating the outstanding credit.
He said the factory was now operating two shifts and had employed more than 2,000 workers, about 80 per cent of whom were women and young school leavers.
President Mahama said such investments demonstrated how development financing could support industrial growth and create employment, particularly for young people.
He urged the bank to sustain its support for businesses in the agriculture and agribusiness sectors, noting that local processors needed adequate financing to purchase raw materials and operate throughout the year.
